card.name: Noun after life-threatening in warnings
card.fires_on: The noun that ends a warning phrase, most often "condition" in "a potentially life-threatening condition" after serotonin syndrome. It also fires on a few other warning nouns such as machinery, addiction, bacteria and harm.

modes.label: Life-threatening condition
modes.description: The word "condition" right after "potentially life-threatening" in serotonin syndrome warnings.
modes.example: Concomitant use of EXXUA with SSRIs or tricyclic antidepressants may cause serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening<< condition>> with changes including altered mental status, hypertension

modes.label: Other warning nouns
modes.description: The closing noun of a short risk phrase, such as machinery, addiction or harm.
modes.example: Plerixafor Injection can cause fetal<< harm>> when administered to a pregnant woman.

card.plain: It marks the last word of a stock warning phrase, especially "condition" after "potentially life-threatening".
